names.explanation: Rahmah shares its root with the womb: the tenderness that carries something helpless without being asked to. Ar-Rahman is that mercy at a scale nothing in creation can hold, and it is unearned and universal. The believer and the denier breathe the same air and eat from the same earth.
names.living: Meet people with more mercy than they have earned from you, because that is exactly how you are being dealt with.

names.explanation: The same root as Ar-Rahman in a different form. Ar-Rahman is mercy as a permanent attribute; Ar-Raheem is mercy in motion, arriving where it is needed. The Quran uses this one for what the believers meet on the Day of Judgment: a specific mercy, delivered to a specific person.
names.living: Ask for it by name. A mercy that acts is a mercy you can ask to act now.

names.explanation: A king owns, commands, and answers to nobody. Every human king borrows those three things and hands them back at death. On the Day of Judgment the question "To whom belongs the sovereignty today?" gets one answer, with no one left to dispute it.
names.living: Whatever authority you hold, over a team or a household or a child, is on loan, and you will be asked how you used it.

names.explanation: Quddus is purity so complete that defect is not a category that applies: no fatigue, no need, no regret, no growing old. It is not that the flaws were removed, it is that there was never a place for them. The angels described their own worship with this root before Adam was made.
names.living: When something in your life goes wrong, the fault is somewhere in the creation, never in the One who made it.

names.explanation: Salam is wholeness: a thing intact, with nothing broken in it. Allah is As-Salam because He is whole in Himself, and because peace reaches His creation from Him and from nowhere else. The greeting Muslims exchange and the words that end every prayer are both built on it.
names.living: Chase peace at its source. Nothing you can buy or arrange will hold what only He gives.

names.explanation: One root gives both faith and safety, because to believe someone is to feel safe with them. Allah is Al-Mumin in both senses: He confirms the truth of what He revealed, and He is the one who makes His servants secure. He testified to His own oneness, and testifies that the believers were right to accept it.
names.living: Put your sense of safety somewhere it cannot be taken from you.

names.explanation: A muhaymin stands over something: watching it, keeping it, and answering for it. Every deed and every word is recorded, and none of that record depends on your memory of it. The Quran uses the same word for itself, standing over the scriptures before it as the standard they are measured by.
names.living: You are never unobserved. That is a warning in private and a comfort when nobody sees the good you do.

names.explanation: Izzah is strength that cannot be worn down and honour that cannot be taken away, so Al-Azeez is the one who is never overcome. In the Quran the name almost always arrives paired, most often as Al-Azeez Al-Hakeem, mighty and wise, because power without wisdom is only force.
names.living: Seek your standing from Him. Honour sought from people has to be renegotiated every day.

names.explanation: The root means to set a broken bone. Al-Jabbar carries both senses at once: the one whose will nothing can resist, and the one who mends what has been broken. The same power nothing escapes is the power that restores.
names.living: When something in you is broken, bring it to the One whose name means both irresistible and mending.

names.explanation: Greatness claimed by a human being is arrogance, because none of it is theirs to claim. In Allah the claim is simply accurate, which makes this the one name whose human imitation is a sin. He is far above resembling anything He made.
names.living: Drop the claim. Everything you would boast about was given to you and can be taken back.

names.explanation: Khalq is bringing something into being on a measure decided in advance. Human making only rearranges what already exists: the carpenter did not grow the tree, and the tree did not invent itself. Allah began with nothing at all.
names.living: Nothing around you arrived by accident, including you.

names.explanation: Where Al-Khaliq is the decision to create, Al-Bari is the execution: bringing the thing out distinct, whole, and exactly to its design. The same root gives the word for recovering from illness, a body returning to the state it was meant to be in.
names.living: You were made deliberately, to a design. You are not an assembly of leftovers.

names.explanation: Surah here means form: the shape and features a created thing ends up wearing. Billions of human faces are built from the same handful of parts and no two of them come out the same. That variation is not a side effect, it is authored.
names.living: Your features were chosen for you by the One who chose them, and He does not choose badly.

names.explanation: The root means to cover. Al-Ghaffar covers a sin so completely that it is hidden in this world and not raised against you in the next. The form is intensive: forgiving again, and again, for the same person and the same sin.
names.living: A repeat offence is not a reason to stop returning. This name is built for repetition.

names.explanation: Qahr is domination so total that resistance is not defeated but impossible. Every power that has ever frightened people, from empires to illness to death itself, is under something else. Al-Qahhar is under nothing.
names.living: Nothing that has power over you has power over Him.

names.explanation: A hibah is a gift given for nothing in return, with no expectation attached to it. Al-Wahhab gives constantly, to everyone, unasked and unrepaid. Sulayman asked for a kingdom nobody after him would hold, and closed the request on this name.
names.living: Ask big. You are asking the one giver who is not weighing what He gets back.

names.explanation: Rizq is much wider than money: health, time, a spouse, a calm mind, and knowledge are all provision. The intensive form means the giving never pauses, and it reaches the one who thanks Him and the one who denies Him on the same morning.
names.living: Work for your provision, but do not confuse the channel it arrives through with the One who sends it.

names.explanation: Fath is an opening: a door, a route through, a verdict that unsticks a dispute. Al-Fattah opens what was closed in the world and in the heart, and the Quran uses the same word for judgment, because a ruling opens a matter that had jammed.
names.living: When every route looks shut, that is precisely the situation this name is for.

names.explanation: His knowledge is not gathered, because it was never absent. The leaf that falls, the seed underground, and the thought you had but did not say are equally present to Him, with no past or future about any of it.
names.living: Ask for knowledge from its source, and be honest even when the truth is known only to you and Him.

names.explanation: Qabd is to close the hand: to withhold, or to take back. Health tightens, income narrows, a heart contracts. The Quran states it in the same breath as its opposite, because the hand that closes is the same hand that opens.
names.living: A narrow season is not neglect. It is one of two hands, and the other one exists.

names.explanation: Bast is to spread the hand open. Provision widens, a chest expands, and a difficulty that had you cornered turns out to have room in it after all. The Quran pairs it with Al-Qabid in a single clause: Allah withholds and grants abundance.
names.living: Ask for expansion in the chest before you ask for expansion in the circumstances.

names.explanation: To lower. Reputations, empires, and the arrogant all come down, and none of them choose the timing. Nothing rises so high that it is out of reach of this name.
names.living: Never build your worth on a position. Positions get lowered.

names.explanation: To raise. Allah raises whoever He wills, and the Quran ties the raising to two things people usually overlook: faith, and knowledge. Yusuf went from the bottom of a well to running a country without a single step of self-promotion.
names.living: The lift that lasts comes from Him, and it tends to arrive through learning and sincerity rather than through positioning.

names.explanation: To give honour. Whoever Allah honours cannot be degraded by anyone, however loudly they try. It is announced in the same verse as its opposite, so neither half can be read on its own.
names.living: If He has honoured you, other people's opinion is noise. If He has not, their approval is worth nothing anyway.

names.explanation: To lower and to humble. Every tyrant in the Quran ends the same way, and not one of them saw it coming. The humbling is not cruelty; it is the removal of a standing that was never earned.
names.living: Fear this one thing: that the way you treat people earns you a lowering you will not see coming.

names.explanation: Hearing without an ear and without limit: every language at once, every voice in a crowd separately, and the dua whispered so quietly that the person beside you missed it. In Arabic, hearing also implies answering, which is why the phrase said on rising from ruku is built on this root.
names.living: You never have to raise your voice, and you never have to wait your turn.

names.explanation: Seeing without an eye: in darkness, through walls, and inside intentions. The Quran tends to place this name at moments of injustice, and the point is always the same. Whatever was done where nobody could see, He saw.
names.living: The good you did where nobody could see it was never actually unwitnessed.

names.explanation: The judge whose verdict is final, because there is no higher court to appeal to and no evidence He was not shown. Human courts get things wrong on incomplete information. This one never rules on a partial file.
names.living: Some wrongs will not be settled in your lifetime. They will still be settled.

names.explanation: Not merely just but justice itself: the standard, rather than something measured against a standard. He never gives less than what is owed, and He remains free to give more, since generosity above what is owed takes nothing from anyone.
names.living: Be fair in the moment when unfairness would be easy and unnoticed.

names.explanation: Lutf is kindness so fine that it goes unnoticed while it happens. The word also means subtlety: reaching what is too small or too hidden for anyone else to get at. Both meanings sit in one name, so His care reaches you at a depth you cannot inspect, by routes you would never have chosen.
names.living: Look back at what you once begged Him to change. Some of it was kindness you could not read at the time.

names.explanation: Khibrah is inside knowledge: not the surface of a thing but its inner workings and what it is really for. Al-Khabir knows the motive underneath the deed, which is why two identical acts of charity are not worth the same.
names.living: Fix the intention. The visible half of your deed was never the half being graded.

names.explanation: Hilm is composure held by someone with every right and every power to retaliate. He is not slow because He is unaware or unable. He delays so that there is time to turn back, and the delay is deliberate.
names.living: The room you have been given to come back was not an oversight. Use it before it closes.

names.explanation: Greatness that actually fills the description, so that anything else called great is being spoken about loosely. Ayat al-Kursi lists what His throne contains and then lands on this name, and it is the word a Muslim says with the spine bent in ruku.
names.living: Bend for the one thing that is genuinely great, and you will stop bending for things that are not.

names.explanation: The same covering as Al-Ghaffar, measured on a different axis: this form is about how much is forgiven rather than how often. No sin is too large for it, which is why the verse forbidding despair of Allah's mercy closes on this name.
names.living: The size of what you did is not the deciding factor. Turning back is.

names.explanation: The one who appreciates. He needs nothing from your worship, and still responds to a small quiet act with a reward out of all proportion to it. He does not discount it for being small.
names.living: Do the tiny consistent thing. It is being noticed, and it is being overpaid.

names.explanation: High above His creation in station, not in location: above being contained, compared, or resembled. The same root names Illiyyin, the highest record kept for the righteous.
names.living: Stop measuring Him against anything you already know. The comparison is the mistake.

names.explanation: Great in status, so that everything else is small by comparison rather than slightly smaller. This is the name behind the takbir, which means every prayer opens by putting the size of your worry next to the size of Allah, out loud.
names.living: Say Allahu akbar and mean the comparison, not just the words.

names.explanation: To guard and to preserve. He guards the creation, He guards the deeds so that none is lost from the record, and He guarded the Quran itself, which is why the text has not shifted in fourteen centuries.
names.living: Guard His limits and you will find yourself guarded. The hadith puts it in exactly those terms.

names.explanation: Qut is the food that keeps a body going: not luxury, but the exact amount required. Al-Muqeet apportions that to every living thing and has the power to deliver it. Nothing alive is fed by accident.
names.living: You are not responsible for producing your sustenance, only for going out honestly to meet it.

names.explanation: Both the reckoner who takes account of everything and the one who suffices, as in hasbi Allah, Allah is enough for me. The two fit together: the one who will settle the account is the one worth relying on.
names.living: Audit yourself now, while the reckoning is still voluntary.

names.explanation: Jalal is the majesty that produces awe rather than affection: greatness of power and station that makes a person go quiet. It is the counterweight to the beauty that draws you closer.
names.living: Awe and love are both owed to Him, and a faith carrying only one of them goes lopsided.

names.explanation: Karam is generosity plus nobility: giving before being asked, giving more than was asked for, and never producing the receipt afterwards. He gives to the one disobeying Him, and conceals what would humiliate them.
names.living: Give the way you would want to be given to: quietly, and without the reminder attached.

names.explanation: A raqib is a watchman posted with unbroken attention. The Quran places this name at moments of accountability between people, over the ties of kinship and over what the Messengers were answerable for.
names.living: Behave in an empty room the way you would behave in a full one.

names.explanation: The one who answers. The Quran states it with no conditions attached: call on Me and I will respond. The response may be the thing asked for, or the thing withheld because it would have harmed you, or the whole of it stored up.
names.living: A dua is never lost. Not answered yet is not the same as not answered.

names.explanation: Vast: in mercy, in knowledge, and in giving. The word is used of something with room in it, and the point of the name is that nothing you bring uses the room up. His mercy is described as having encompassed all things.
names.living: Never assume you have spent your share. The vessel does not run low.

names.explanation: Hikmah is putting each thing exactly where it belongs at exactly the right time. Wisdom is why His decree can look wrong from inside it: you are reading one page of the reasoning and drawing a conclusion about the book.
names.living: When the reason is withheld, trust the one holding it. That is what this name is for.

names.explanation: Wudd is love that shows itself: affection expressed, not merely felt. The Quran names the people He loves out loud, those who turn back to Him, who keep themselves clean, who act well. He also places that love for you in other people's hearts.
names.living: You are not merely tolerated by your Lord. Live like someone who is loved.

names.explanation: Majd is greatness and generosity in one word: high in station, and open-handed with it. Power that hoards is not majd. The Quran applies the word both to Allah and to itself.
names.living: Height without generosity is only distance.

names.explanation: To raise up and to send out. The name covers both the resurrection of the dead and the sending of the Messengers, because both are life arriving where there was none. The Quran argues from one to the other by pointing at dead ground turning green.
names.living: Nothing about you is past reviving, including the parts you have already written off.

names.explanation: A witness who was present, saw it, and will testify. Nothing has to be reconstructed after the fact. On the Day of Judgment even limbs will speak, and not one word of it will be new information to Him.
names.living: You already have a witness to the wrong done to you, and to the wrong you did.

names.explanation: Haqq is truth in the sense of reality: what actually is, as against what merely appears. Everything else exists on loan and will stop. His existence is not borrowed from anywhere, which makes Him the standard for what real means.
names.living: Anchor to what is real. Most of what competes for your life will not be there at the end of it.

names.explanation: A wakeel is the agent you hand a matter to because they can handle it better than you can. Tawakkul is doing that with Allah: taking your means seriously and then genuinely letting go of the outcome.
names.living: Tie your camel, then hand over the result and stop rehearsing it at night.

names.explanation: Strength complete in itself, with no source behind it. Human strength is always borrowed from food, sleep, youth, or numbers, and all four run out. His draws on nothing.
names.living: There is no balance of forces in which asking Him becomes pointless.

names.explanation: Matin is firm and unyielding: strength that does not tire or slacken with use. Al-Qawiyy is the amount of the strength, Al-Matin is its steadiness over time.
names.living: He will not get tired of you asking. Only people run out of patience for that.

names.explanation: A wali is a close ally who protects you and manages your affairs. Allah is the wali of those who believe, bringing them out of darkness into light, and the word for those closest to Him comes straight from this name.
names.living: Take Him as your ally first, and be careful whose alliance you take instead.

names.explanation: Praiseworthy in Himself, whether or not anyone is praising Him. Human praise is a response to a performance; His praiseworthiness does not depend on an audience or on an occasion.
names.living: Say alhamdulillah in the season you would rather complain about. He is Hameed in both.

names.explanation: To count exactly, item by item, leaving nothing out. He has enumerated all things in number: every atom, every breath, every deed and its weight. The hadith about the ninety-nine names uses this same root for what a person does with them.
names.living: No good you did was too small to be counted. Nothing else was either.

names.explanation: The one who begins. Every created thing had a first instant it did not choose and could not have arranged. Origination is the harder of the two acts, and He does it first.
names.living: You did not start yourself, so the terms of your existence were never yours to set.

names.explanation: The one who brings back. This is the Quran's own argument for the resurrection: repeating something is easier than beginning it, and the beginning has already happened once in front of you.
names.living: The return is not a strange idea. It is the simpler half of something already done.

names.explanation: The giver of life: to a body, to the earth after rain, and to a heart that had gone hard. The Quran points at dead ground turning green and asks you to draw the obvious conclusion about yourself.
names.living: A heart can be revived the way land is. Ask for the rain.

names.explanation: The one who causes death, at an appointed time that does not move forward or back. In the Quran death is not an accident or a failure of the system. It is an appointment, and it is created, exactly as life is.
names.living: Death is scheduled, so the useful question is not when, it is what you will be doing.

names.explanation: Alive with a life unlike ours: not sustained by anything, not begun, not ending. Our life is a loan of a few decades. His is what the word life meant before it was lent to anyone.
names.living: Ya Hayyu ya Qayyum is the dua of someone who has reached the end of their own resources.

names.explanation: Self-sustaining, and sustaining everything else at the same time. Nothing continues for a moment except by His holding it there. Ayat al-Kursi opens on these two names together, and everything the verse says afterwards follows from them.
names.living: You are being held up right now by something you are not doing yourself.

names.explanation: The one who finds whatever He seeks and lacks nothing at all. Nothing is missing from Him and nothing is out of reach, so He never has to make do with a substitute.
names.living: He is never short of the thing you are asking for.

names.explanation: The same majd as Al-Majeed, in a form that stresses the quality as an established attribute rather than a description applied to Him. Nobility and generosity as one thing: glory that gives.
names.living: Approach Him expecting generosity, because the name says the greatness and the giving are the same.

names.explanation: One with no second, no partner, no rival, and no equal in any attribute. This is the claim the Quran argues for hardest, because everything else in the religion follows from it.
names.living: Divide your worship and it stops being worship. This name does not share.

names.explanation: Related to Al-Wahid but sharper: one and indivisible, not assembled from parts, so He cannot be split, added to, or reduced. The Quran uses this exact form once, to open Surah Al-Ikhlas.
names.living: Do not picture Him. Anything you can picture is made of parts.

names.explanation: Samad is the one everyone turns to in need and who needs no one: solid, with no hollow in it. Everything else in existence depends on something further along. He is where the chain of dependence stops.
names.living: Every need you have ends up at Him anyway. Save yourself the detours.

names.explanation: Able: holding power over anything He wills, with nothing able to interrupt it. The same root gives qadar, the decree, because His power and His measuring out are one act rather than two.
names.living: The word impossible describes your reach, not His.

names.explanation: The intensive of Al-Qadir: power exercised and prevailing, not merely held in reserve. The Quran reaches for this form when describing a people taken at the height of their confidence.
names.living: Confidence in your own position is only safe when it is actually confidence in Him.

names.explanation: The one who puts forward. Some people, some events, and some answers to dua are advanced ahead of others, and the ordering is His. What arrives early arrived early on purpose.
names.living: What came to you sooner than you deserved was placed there.

names.explanation: The one who delays. He postpones a punishment that was already due, and He holds back things you asked for until the moment they would be good for you rather than harmful.
names.living: A delay is a decision, not the absence of one.

names.explanation: The First, with nothing before Him. Not the earliest item in a sequence but outside the sequence altogether, since time is itself created. There is no before to put Him after.
names.living: He was there before the problem, and before the person who caused it.

names.explanation: The Last, with nothing after Him. Everything you can name has an end, including the things that look permanent from here. He is what remains once the list is finished.
names.living: Invest in what survives the ending. Almost nothing does.

names.explanation: The Manifest: above everything, and evident through everything He made. The Prophet paired this name with the next one in a single dua, and the pairing is the point.
names.living: The evidence is not scarce. Look at anything closely enough.

names.explanation: The Hidden: not distant but nearer than what is visible, beyond the reach of sight and imagination. He knows the inside of things, and the Quran places Him closer to you than the vein in your neck.
names.living: Nearness and invisibility are not opposites here.

names.explanation: The governor: the one who owns things and actually runs them. Not an absent owner collecting rent, but the one directing the affair moment by moment.
names.living: Nothing is running unattended, including the part of your life that feels unattended.

names.explanation: Supremely exalted, far above the limits and comparisons people try to place on Him. The form is emphatic: high, and then higher than the description itself manages to reach.
names.living: When someone reduces God to something manageable, that is not the God this name describes.

names.explanation: Birr is doing good expansively and kindly, and it is the same word the Quran uses for how children should treat their parents. Al-Barr is the source of all of it, kind to His servants far beyond what any of them are owed.
names.living: The birr you show your parents is a small copy of the birr being shown to you.

names.explanation: Tawbah is turning back, and the Quran uses the word of Allah in both directions. He turns to the servant so that the servant becomes able to turn to Him, and then He turns to them again in acceptance. Your repentance was His gift before it was your act.
names.living: The fact that you want to return is already the first half of the answer.

names.explanation: The one who exacts retribution from those who persisted after every warning. In the Quran the word always describes a specific reckoning at the end of a long refusal, never a temper.
names.living: Do not envy someone who appears to be getting away with it. Nobody gets away with it.

names.explanation: Afw goes a step past forgiveness: it erases. Al-Ghafoor covers the sin, Al-Afuw removes the record of it. When Aisha asked what to say on Laylat al-Qadr, the Prophet taught her a dua built on this name.
names.living: Ask to have it erased, not only hidden: Allahumma innaka afuwwun tuhibbul-afwa fa'fu anni.

names.explanation: Rafah is the tenderest form of mercy: the kind that cannot bear to watch suffering. It is why obligations arrived in stages, why hardship excuses exist in the law, and why the Quran describes the Prophet himself with this word toward the believers.
names.living: The religion was made bearable on purpose. Take the concessions He gave you.

names.explanation: Owner of all sovereignty. He gives dominion to whoever He wills and takes it from whoever He wills, He honours and He humbles, and the verse ends by saying all good is in His hand. Kingdoms change hands on His decision, not on their own strength.
names.living: Whatever you hold was handed to you, and will be handed on.

names.root: ج ل ل / ك ر م
names.explanation: Possessor of majesty and honour: the two halves of how He is known. Jalal is the greatness that makes you fall silent, ikram is the generosity that makes you come closer. Surah Ar-Rahman closes on this name after asking seventy-eight times which favour you would deny.
names.living: Fear Him without running from Him. The name holds both at once.

names.explanation: Qist is equity: giving each party exactly their due, especially when settling something between them. Allah loves those who deal in qist and He judges by it, so nobody is shortchanged for being unpopular or unimportant.
names.living: Be equitable in the ruling that costs you something. That is the only kind that counts.

names.explanation: The gatherer. He gathers all of creation on a day there is no doubt about, He gathers scattered people back into each other's lives, and He gathers opposites inside one heart.
names.living: Nothing scattered is beyond gathering, including a life that has come apart.

names.explanation: Rich in the absolute sense: needing nothing from anyone. Your worship adds nothing to Him and your sin takes nothing from Him. The benefit in this relationship runs in one direction only.
names.living: You do not do Him a favour by praying. The favour was the invitation.

names.explanation: The enricher: He makes others rich out of His own richness, so any independence a human being has is something received. Wealth of the heart is the real form of it, and that is His to give as well.
names.living: Ask for enough, and for the contentment that makes enough feel like enough.

names.explanation: The withholder. What He prevents from reaching you does not reach you, and prevention is protection as often as it is denial. The words said after every prayer put it plainly: none can withhold what You give, none can give what You withhold.
names.living: The thing you did not get was blocked deliberately, by someone who knew what was inside it.

names.explanation: The one who allows harm to reach whom He wills, always inside a purpose. Nothing hurts you outside His knowledge, and no harm arrives merely to hurt. A loss can be a correction, a debt cleared, or a door shutting so that another one opens.
names.living: If harm can only arrive by His permission, the one to ask for relief is the one who permitted it.

names.explanation: The one who allows benefit to reach whom He wills. It is paired with Ad-Darr on purpose, because a Muslim treats both as coming from the same hand, and neither as coming from a person, an object, or a date on the calendar.
names.living: Thank the people who help you, and stay clear about where the help came from.

names.explanation: Light of the heavens and the earth: by Him things are seen, and by Him hearts see. Ordinary light shows you the room. This light shows you what to do with your life.
names.living: Ask for light. Knowledge without it is just information.

names.explanation: The guide. He shows the way, and He also makes a heart accept it, which are two different acts. The Prophet was told plainly that he could not guide the person he loved most; only Allah does that part.
names.living: You can show someone the way. Stop carrying the part that was never yours.

names.explanation: The originator of the heavens and the earth: inventor of what had no precedent, made after no model, because there was no model. Everything human beings call original is a recombination of something already lying around.
names.living: Your situation has no precedent to you. It presents no difficulty to Him.

names.explanation: The one who remains. Everyone on the earth will perish and the face of your Lord will remain: that is the entire comparison, drawn by the Quran in two verses, with nothing else added.
names.living: Put your effort where it will still exist. Very little qualifies.

names.explanation: The inheritor. After every owner is gone, ownership returns to the one it never actually left. Zakariyya used this name while asking for a child, adding that Allah is the best of inheritors either way.
names.living: Everything you own is on its way to someone else, and then back to Him.

names.explanation: Rushd is soundness of judgment: seeing the right course and taking it. Ar-Rasheed directs His creation along that course, and the verse carrying this name contrasts guidance with error so clearly that it concludes there is no need to compel anyone in religion.
names.living: Ask for rushd before you ask for a specific outcome. You may be asking for the wrong thing.

names.explanation: Patient without limit, and without any of the strain that patience costs a human being. He does not hurry the punishment of those who have earned it, because nothing forces His hand and no moment can slip past Him.
names.living: His patience with you is the model for yours with everyone else.
